bib.title: Lessons from the Trenches on Reproducible Evaluation of Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Lessons from the Trenches on Reproducible Evaluation of Language Models", Stella Biderman, Hailey Schoelkopf, Lintang Sutawika (lead authors, all EleutherAI as printed) plus 27 others. No venue is printed; the only marking is the arXiv stamp "arXiv:2405.14782v3 [cs.CL] 31 May 2026", so treat it as a preprint (v3). A NeurIPS-style author checklist is attached, but no venue is named.

File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/08-eval/sources/biderman-2024-lessons-trenches-reproducible-evaluation-language.pdf

COVERAGE: 31 of 31 pages, 123,581 chars. Pages 1-11 (main text) and 21-31 (checklist, Appendices A-G) were read in full. Pages 11-21 (references) were skimmed only by keyword scan for odd text.

CLAIMS (ranked)

1. Prompt format alone moves accuracy by more than 20 points and changes model rankings.
   - setup: 0-shot, loglikelihood multiple choice, lm-eval v0.4.2, 5 open models, ARC-Challenge (Cloze vs MMLU-style) and MMLU (Hybrid vs MMLU-style). The ± values are 95% bootstrap CIs. Single run per cell.
   - quote (p5, Table 1; column order ARC Cloze, ARC MMLU-style, MMLU Hybrid, MMLU MMLU-style): "GPT-NeoX-20B38.0±2.78%26.6±2.53%27.6±0.74%24.5±0.71% / Llama-2-7B43.5±2.84%42.8±2.83%39.8±0.79%41.3±0.80% / Falcon-7B40.2±2.81%25.9±2.51%29.1±0.75%25.4±0.72% / Mistral-7B50.1±2.86%72.4±2.56%48.3±0.80%58.6±0.77% / Mixtral-8x7B56.7±2.84%81.3±2.23%59.7±0.77%67.1±0.72%"
   - quote (p5): "performance varies dramatically with the prompt(in some cases, >20% ), andwhich prompt style works best varies by model."
   - Direction flips by model: Mistral and Mixtral gain about 22-25 points on ARC with MMLU-style, while NeoX and Falcon lose about 11-14.

2. The most extreme case is ARC-Easy with GPT-NeoX-20B.
   - quote (p9): "using the “cloze” evaluation setup, GPT-NeoX achieves an accuracy of72.4±1.80% but using the MMLU-style setup it scores26.5±1.78%."
   - Cause, from inspecting completions: the model fails to follow the output format, not the task. Supported by observation only; no numbers given.

3. Single-run point estimates mislead.
   - setup: not the authors' experiment. GPQA, OpenAI and Anthropic models, data from Lukošiūtė (2024). No numeric values are printed in the text.
   - quote (p9): "Presenting single-run point estimates of performance (top) instead of a 95% confidence interval across 10 runs of the benchmark (bottom) paints a very different pictures".
   - Also p9: HumanEval "contains only 164 examples", so small gains "might be washed out simply via sampling again at the same temperature."

4. Aggregation choice matters.
   - MMLU micro-average vs macro-average over "57 subjects" (p6): "affects results by several percentage points". No exact figure.
   - Dataset quirks (p6): ARC has one 5-choice question; HumanEval has 3 documents lacking example tests.

5. Implementations disagree (second-hand, no numbers).
   - Fourrier et al. (2023b): HELM, lm-eval and the original MMLU code give "widely different scores and even change the ranking order" (p5).
   - Lyu et al. (2024): loglikelihood MCQ and generative MCQ scoring "do not even agree" (p8).

6. Leaderboard gaming (p9, anecdotal).
   - Open LLM Leaderboard entrants fine-tuned to the harness format, "targeting separator tokens used in particular versions of lm-eval".

7. Answer extraction (p28, no experiment).
   - Regex extraction biases toward models that match the original format.
   - quote: "it is difficult to separate models’ compliance with the evaluationformatfrom their answercorrectness."

8. "The Key Problem" framing (p2).
   - The best automated tools for judging semantic equivalence "are the very models we are seeking to evaluate".
   - Three responses: closed-domain conversion (MCQ, string match, verifier), model-based grading, human labour.

RECOMMENDED PRACTICES (exact headings)

- Section 3.2 (p7):
  - "Provide Evaluation Code"
  - "Provide Prompts and Detail Methodology Thoroughly", including "the amount of prompt engineering performed and on which models and evaluation sets", loglikelihood and perplexity hyperparameters, generation hyperparameters, and answer-extraction heuristics
  - "Create Reporting Standards"
- Section 4.2 (p10):
  - "Perform Statistical Analyses, and Report on Sources of Variance and Error"
  - "Evaluate Models in Realistic Settings"
  - "Do Exploratory Analysis to Build Better Understanding of Results"
- Appendix D checklist (pp30-31):
  - "Always share your exact prompts." With it: "Prompts should not be optimized for performance on a given model, and the amount of prompt engineering done should be disclosed."
  - "Avoid copying results from other implementations."
  - "Always provide model outputs." Reasons given: lets others recompute scores and run significance tests, and reproduces API results after deprecation.
  - "Perform qualitative analyses." Review a small batch before running at scale.
  - "Perform statistical significance testing." Includes more than one seed, or "averaging over multiple selections of few-shot examples".

WHAT lm-eval DOES

- Standard errors: "We report bootstrapped standard error metrics by default" (p10). The authors distinguish this question-sampling variance from run-to-run variance; both are held to matter, as is prompt variance.
- Prompts: a one-line YAML change; the task config plus library version is the reporting unit; PromptSource multiprompt evaluation is supported.
- Outputs: `--limit` for dry runs and `--log_samples` for per-sample scores and saved outputs (p8).
- Extraction: per-task `Filter` chains (p28).
- MCQ scoring: `acc` (raw loglikelihood), `acc_norm` (byte-length normalised), `acc_mutual_info` (p25).
- Perplexity: bits per byte, word-level and byte-level; non-overlapping windows (pp26-27).
- Few-shot: drawn from the fewshot split, then train, then validation, then test (p29); the MMLU config uses `sampler: first_n`.
- Defaults priority (p7): model trainers' consensus, then the official implementation, then evaluators' consensus, then the maintainers' preference.
- Tokenisation: trailing prompt whitespace is moved into the target string (p25).

LIMITS

- Only one original experiment: 5 models, 2-3 tasks, 0-shot, one run each, on 8x A40 in under a day.
- No experiment on few-shot selection, answer extraction, normalisation method, sampling temperature, or run-to-run variance; all of these are asserted via citations.
- Scope is MCQ-centric by the authors' own admission (p3). LLM judges get one paragraph; agents are not covered.
- Appendix F (Limitations) is truncated in the PDF itself: "There are additionally more case studies and concrete instances of our discussed". It concedes that measurement validity is not treated in depth.
- All models tested are 2022-23 open-weight models.

BUILDS ON: Gao et al. (2023) lm-eval; Brown et al. (2020) loglikelihood MCQ and cloze prompts; Gao (2021) normalisation; Press et al. (2020) strided perplexity; Dehghani et al. (2021) Benchmark Lottery; Marie et al. (2021); Card et al. (2020); Lukošiūtė (2024); Fourrier et al. (2023b); Alzahrani et al. (2024); Sclar et al. (2023); Bach et al. (2022) PromptSource.

CODE: YAML configs on pp29-30. The extraction is letter-spaced, so this is reconstructed rather than verbatim. Cloze: `doc_to_text: "Question: {{question}}\nAnswer:"` with `doc_to_choice: "{{choices.text}}"`. MMLU-style: `doc_to_choice: ["A","B","C","D"]`. Hybrid: same prompt with `doc_to_choice: choices`.

FIGURES: one candidate, Figure 2 (p9), GPQA single run vs 95% CI over ten runs. It shows the ranking dissolving once intervals are drawn, which suits 09-reading-results. The data is third-party (Lukošiūtė).

PROBLEMS

- No embedded instructions found.
- The arXiv stamp reads "31 May 2026" for v3, a later revision than the 2024 original; contents may differ from v1 (for example the mentions of Dunlap 2024 and Vibe-Eval).
- The text calls the table "Table 3.1"; its caption says "Table 1".
- Table cells are fused without spaces; the column order was taken from the header.
- The printed flag "--log samples" lost its underscore in extraction.
- Typo in the source: "on the rd".
- Figure 2 values are image-only and were not extracted.
